limitations_and_boundaries: Assumes causal sufficiency (no hidden confounding variables).
Assumes samples for a given interventional distribution are independent and identically distributed.
Assumes causal relationships form an acyclic graph (no feedback loops).
Theoretical results are valid in the infinite-data regime.
Performance sensitive to hyperparameter controlling DAG sparsity; selected by maximizing held-out likelihood for score-based methods, but constraint-based methods use a fixed cutoff.
DCDI-DSF advantage over DCDI-G is marginal in the evaluated settings.
GIES outperforms DCDI on linear Gaussian data, which matches its assumptions.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

research_questions.statement: Can a continuous-constrained optimization framework leverage interventional data to improve causal discovery?

provenance.text_excerpt: We illustrate the flexibility of the continuous-constrained framework by taking advantage of expressive neural architectures such as normalizing flows.

claims.statement: The continuous-constrained framework is flexible and can take advantage of expressive neural architectures such as normalizing flows.

provenance.text_excerpt: This work constitutes a new step in this direction by proposing a theoretically-grounded method based on neural networks that can leverage interventional data.

claims.statement: The proposed method can leverage interventional data to alleviate identifiability issues in causal discovery.

experiments_or_tasks: Propose a theoretically-grounded method based on neural networks that can leverage interventional data for causal discovery.

methods.name: DCDI
methods.protocol_description: A continuous constrained optimization method for causal discovery from interventional data, using neural networks and normalizing flows. It reformulates the combinatorial DAG search as a continuous optimization problem solved via the augmented Lagrangian method, incorporating interventional data to improve identifiability.

study_units.name: DCDI method proposal

provenance.text_excerpt: In Appendix C.2, we show cases where DCDI-G fails to detect the right causal direction due to its lack of capacity, whereas DCDI-DSF systematically succeeds.

claims.statement: DCDI-G fails to detect the right causal direction in some cases due to lack of capacity, whereas DCDI-DSF systematically succeeds.

provenance.text_excerpt: While the advantage of DCDI-DSF over DCDI-G is marginal, it might be explained by the fact that the densities can be sufficiently well modeled by DCDI-G.

claims.statement: The advantage of DCDI-DSF over DCDI-G is marginal, possibly because densities can be sufficiently well modeled by DCDI-G.

provenance.text_excerpt: For all intervention settings, DCDI has overall the best performance.

claims.statement: DCDI has overall the best performance across all intervention settings.

datasets.description: Synthetic data generated from 20-node graphs with different intervention types (perfect, imperfect, perfect unknown) and varying edge densities (e=1, e=4).
datasets.name: Synthetic interventional data

experiments_or_tasks: Evaluate DCDI against baseline methods on synthetic data with perfect, imperfect, and perfect unknown interventions.

methods.name: DCDI-G
methods.protocol_description: A variant of DCDI using Gaussian conditionals.

methods.name: DCDI-DSF
methods.protocol_description: A variant of DCDI using deep sigmoidal flows for conditionals.

methods.name: GIES
methods.protocol_description: Greedy Interventional Equivalence Search, a score-based method assuming linear Gaussian models and optimizing BIC over I-Markov equivalence classes.

methods.name: CAM
methods.protocol_description: Causal Additive Models, modified to support interventions.

methods.name: IGSP
methods.protocol_description: Interventional Greedy Sparsest Permutation, a constraint-based method using conditional independence tests.

methods.name: UT-IGSP
methods.protocol_description: Unknown Target IGSP, an extension of IGSP for interventions with unknown targets.
